text: Patient is a 85 year old male complaining of dry cough and hoarseness of voice since yesterday. The patient did not experience wheeze. Had a course of tiotropium once daily for 3 months two months ago with partial relief. Triage vitals were as follows: SpO2 95% on room air, BP 173/94 mmHg, heart rate 100 bpm. Result of high-resolution CT thorax is pending at the time of writing. Surgical history: NIV and bronchoscopy.

32-year-old female admitted with dyspnoea, chest pain and deformity of the limb. Over the past few days the patient has had dizziness with occasional pedal oedema. Absence of melaena noted. Previous episodes of exertional fatigue in 2022 resolved without treatment. There is a strong family history of myocardial infarction. Patient is not on ramipril.
Patient is on bisoprolol, 5 mg orally once daily. EKG was performed, showing an irregularly irregular rhythm at 118 bpm. Suspected hypertension versus deep vein thrombosis.
Findings are consistent with aortic stenosis. Patient was shifted to the ward after stenting.

44-year-old male admitted with unintentional weight loss, cold intolerance and constipation. There is a strong family history of primary hyperparathyroidism. Patient is not on carbimazole. Result of oral glucose tolerance test is pending at the time of writing. Suspected cholelithiasis versus DKA. Surgical history: wound debridement and fine needle aspiration cytology.

Patient is a 80 year old female complaining of night sweats and dry cough since yesterday. Over the past few days the patient has had breathlessness on exertion with occasional knee pain. The patient did not experience hoarseness of voice.
Previous episodes of pleuritic chest pain in 2013 resolved without treatment. The patient's sister has pneumothorax. Administered ceftriaxone 1 g IV in the department. Physical examination showed chest tightness; SpO2 95% on room air, BP 172/70 mmHg, heart rate 80 bpm.
Result of arterial blood gas is pending at the time of writing. Rule out acute bronchitis. Known pleural effusion, currently under treatment. Surgeons recommended bronchoscopy and bariatric surgery. Will proceed to non-invasive ventilation if high-resolution CT thorax is abnormal.

Patient is a 39 year old female complaining of muscle weakness and persistent cough since yesterday. On direct questioning, the patient admitted to wheezing. Patient is on amoxicillin-clavulanate, 625 mg PO TDS. Surgeons recommended wound suturing and thrombolysis.

70-year-old male admitted with high-grade fever, altered mental status and loss of consciousness. Over the past few days the patient has had vomiting with occasional seizure. The patient did not experience profuse sweating. Triage vitals were as follows: SpO2 93% on room air, BP 173/104 mmHg, heart rate 118 bpm. CT head was performed, showing no acute abnormality. Surgeons recommended liver biopsy and cardiopulmonary resuscitation.

Patient is a 39 year old female complaining of seizure and haematemesis since yesterday. Over the past few days the patient has had bleeding from the wound with occasional loss of consciousness. Absence of high-grade fever noted. Previous episodes of difficulty breathing in 2010 resolved without treatment. There is a strong family history of organophosphate poisoning. Administered morphine 5 mg IV in the department. Electrocardiogram was performed, showing ST depression in the anterior leads.
Suspected sepsis versus interstitial lung disease. Known anaphylaxis, currently under treatment. Surgical history: nasogastric tube insertion and suturing of the wound. Patient was shifted to the ward after ICD insertion.

Patient is a 85 year old male complaining of generalised weakness and epigastric pain since yesterday.
On direct questioning, the patient admitted to jaundice. Absence of loss of consciousness noted. Previously hospitalized with Parkinson disease in 2006.
Administered ceftriaxone 2 g intravenously in the department.
Carotid Doppler was performed, showing no haemodynamically significant narrowing. Suspected migraine versus epilepsy. Known GBS, currently under treatment.
Surgeons recommended LP and burr hole drainage. Patient was shifted to the ward after mechanical thrombectomy.

82-year-old female admitted with loss of consciousness, haematemesis and resting tremor. On direct questioning, the patient admitted to facial droop. Absence of forgetfulness noted. Patient is on sumatriptan, 50 mg orally PRN. Physical examination showed slurred speech; HR 90 bpm, BP 129/81 mmHg, RR 23/min, temp 103 F. Findings are consistent with Bell's palsy.

Patient is a 56 year old male complaining of low back pain and deformity of the limb since yesterday. Had a course of etoricoxib once daily for 1 week two months ago with partial relief. Physical examination showed sciatica; SpO2 90% on room air, BP 141/65 mmHg, heart rate 94 bpm. Findings are consistent with gout. Surgeons recommended microdiscectomy and arthroscopic ACL reconstruction.

Patient is a 70 year old female complaining of dysuria and blurred vision since yesterday. Over the past few days the patient has had pallor with occasional resting tremor. Known CKD, currently under treatment.

Patient is a 61 year old male complaining of abdominal distension and epigastric pain since yesterday. There is a strong family history of anaphylaxis. Surgical history: colonoscopy and surgical debridement.

22-year-old male admitted with rigors, loss of appetite and pyrexia. Over the past few days the patient has had dizziness with occasional weight loss. Absence of generalized weakness noted. Previous episodes of night sweats in 2000 resolved without treatment. There is a strong family history of ICH. Patient is not on telmisartan. Patient is on co-amoxiclav, 625 mg PO TDS.
Result of malaria rapid antigen test is pending at the time of writing. Suspected high blood pressure versus UTI. Surgical history: blood transfusion and peripheral IV cannulation. Will proceed to lumbar puncture if abdominal ultrasound is abnormal.

Patient is a 55 year old female complaining of excessive thirst and heat intolerance since yesterday. On direct questioning, the patient admitted to irregular menstrual cycles. Previous episodes of polyuria in 2021 resolved without treatment. Administered sitagliptin 100 mg PO in the department. Suspected diabetic neuropathy versus T2DM. Surgeons recommended parathyroidectomy and total thyroidectomy. Patient was shifted to the ward after burr hole drainage.

Patient is a 86 year old male complaining of heat intolerance and epigastric pain since yesterday. Triage vitals were as follows: HR 119 bpm, BP 161/97 mmHg, RR 24/min, temp 98 F. Oral glucose tolerance test was performed, showing a 2-hour value of 212 mg/dL. Findings are consistent with type 1 diabetes mellitus.

47-year-old male admitted with restricted movement, hoarseness of voice and inability to bear weight. On direct questioning, the patient admitted to morning stiffness. Previous episodes of deformity of the limb in 2001 resolved without treatment. Result of urinalysis is pending at the time of writing. Rule out rotator cuff tear. Findings are consistent with unstable angina. Will proceed to open reduction and internal fixation if cerebrospinal fluid analysis is abnormal.

Patient is a 86 year old male complaining of weight gain and blurred vision since yesterday. Over the past few days the patient has had palpitations with occasional polyuria. Previously hospitalized with hyperthyroidism in 2006. Patient is on insulin aspart, 6 units SC three times daily. Result of TSH is pending at the time of writing.

84-year-old male admitted with left arm pain, wheeze and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea. The patient did not experience orthopnoea. There is a strong family history of dyslipidemia. Surgeons recommended CABG and aortic valve replacement.

Patient is a 71 year old female complaining of knee pain and joint swelling since yesterday. On direct questioning, the patient admitted to morning stiffness. Suspected lumbar disc prolapse versus ACL tear. Findings are consistent with tibial shaft fracture. Surgical history: lumbar microdiscectomy and knee arthroscopy. Will proceed to surgical debridement if CT scan of the wrist is abnormal.

Patient is a 54 year old female complaining of knee pain and joint tenderness since yesterday.
The patient did not experience LBP. Previous episodes of difficulty breathing in 2000 resolved without treatment. Had a course of cefazolin every 8 hours for 2 days two months ago with partial relief. Administered naproxen 500 mg orally in the department.
Triage vitals were as follows: SpO2 93% on room air, BP 107/88 mmHg, heart rate 73 bpm. MRI lumbar spine was performed, showing a posterolateral disc bulge at L4-L5 compressing the nerve root. Findings are consistent with anterior cruciate ligament tear. Surgical history: plaster of Paris cast application and microdiscectomy. Will proceed to closed reduction if glycosylated hemoglobin is abnormal.

26-year-old male admitted with fever, chest tightness and night sweats. On direct questioning, the patient admitted to dyspnoea. Absence of polydipsia noted. Previously hospitalized with community-acquired pneumonia in 2001. The patient's sister has pleural effusion.
Had a course of rifampicin OD for 6 months two months ago with partial relief. Patient is on ondansetron, 4 mg intravenously TDS. Sputum culture was performed, showing growth of a gram-positive organism. Rule out bronchogenic carcinoma.
Known COPD, currently under treatment.

63-year-old male admitted with bleeding from the wound, profuse sweating and seizure. Over the past few days the patient has had difficulty breathing with occasional chest pain. The patient did not experience vomiting. Previously hospitalized with pneumonia in 2003. Patient is not on ceftriaxone. Patient is on naloxone, 0.4 mg intravenously stat.
Physical examination showed severe abdominal pain; SpO2 90% on room air, BP 159/82 mmHg, heart rate 73 bpm. Result of chest X-ray is pending at the time of writing. Suspected sepsis versus traumatic brain injury. Known status epilepticus, currently under treatment.
Surgical history: intercostal drain insertion and endotracheal intubation.
Patient was shifted to the ward after gastric lavage.

31-year-old male admitted with loss of consciousness, profuse sweating and severe abdominal pain. Absence of high-grade fever noted. Had a course of ondansetron every 8 hours for 1 day two months ago with partial relief. Patient is on adrenaline, 0.5 mg IM stat. Known traumatic brain injury, currently under treatment. Surgical history: ERCP and splinting. Patient was shifted to the ward after gastric lavage.

Patient is a 20 year old female complaining of wheezing and persistent cough since yesterday. On direct questioning, the patient admitted to haemoptysis. The patient did not experience breathlessness on exertion.
Previous episodes of pleuritic chest pain in 1999 resolved without treatment. Had a course of ipratropium QID for 3 days two months ago with partial relief. Administered co-amoxiclav 625 mg orally in the department. Tuberculin skin test was performed, showing an induration of 16 mm. Rule out interstitial lung disease. Known knee osteoarthritis, currently under treatment.
Surgeons recommended chest drain insertion and thoracentesis. Will proceed to tracheostomy if sputum AFB smear is abnormal.

24-year-old male admitted with hip pain, difficulty walking and sciatica. The patient did not experience joint swelling. Known rotator cuff tear, currently under treatment. Surgeons recommended total hip replacement and total knee arthroplasty. Will proceed to knee arthroscopy if RF is abnormal.

Patient is a 32 year old female complaining of pallor and nausea since yesterday. The patient did not experience weight loss. Patient is not on ceftriaxone. Findings are consistent with malaria. Surgical history: peripheral IV cannulation and blood transfusion.

61-year-old male admitted with icterus, melaena and heartburn. The patient did not experience chest tightness. Administered mesalazine 800 mg orally in the department. Physical examination showed hematemesis; HR 123 bpm, BP 119/67 mmHg, RR 25/min, temp 97 F. Known appendicitis, currently under treatment. Surgical history: appendectomy and liver biopsy.

Patient is a 30 year old male complaining of body aches and photophobia since yesterday. On direct questioning, the patient admitted to neck stiffness. The patient did not experience numbness. Previously hospitalized with congestive heart failure in 2000. There is a strong family history of Parkinson's disease. Had a course of ceftriaxone twice daily for 10 days two months ago with partial relief. Patient is on dexamethasone, 10 mg intravenously QID. Rule out migraine. Findings are consistent with bacterial meningitis.
Surgeons recommended decompressive craniectomy and mechanical thrombectomy.
Patient was shifted to the ward after intravenous thrombolysis.

31-year-old female admitted with numbness, vertigo and joint tenderness. The patient did not experience profuse sweating. Previously hospitalized with bacterial meningitis in 2022. The patient's sister has Alzheimer's disease.
Patient is not on ASA.
Patient is on levetiracetam, 1000 mg IV twice daily. Physical examination showed headache; SpO2 92% on room air, BP 152/67 mmHg, heart rate 121 bpm.
MRI of the brain was performed, showing no focal lesion. Rule out peripheral neuropathy. Known TIA, currently under treatment. Surgical history: mechanical thrombectomy and LP. Will proceed to decompressive craniectomy if non-contrast CT brain is abnormal.

Patient is a 70 year old female complaining of shortness of breath and productive cough since yesterday. On direct questioning, the patient admitted to confusion.
Absence of high-grade fever noted.
Previous episodes of polyuria in 2012 resolved without treatment.
Patient is not on furosemide.
Patient is on ramipril, 2.5 mg PO once daily.
Physical examination showed left arm pain; SpO2 92% on room air, BP 177/79 mmHg, heart rate 72 bpm. Blood culture was performed, showing growth of a gram-negative organism. Suspected IDA versus pericarditis.
Findings are consistent with unstable angina. Surgical history: cardioversion and pacemaker implantation. Will proceed to coronary artery bypass grafting if electrocardiogram is abnormal.

Patient is a 81 year old male complaining of syncope and orthopnea since yesterday.
On direct questioning, the patient admitted to profuse sweating.
The patient did not experience giddiness. Previously hospitalized with DKA in 2003. Administered atorvastatin 40 mg PO in the department.
Physical examination showed fatigue; HR 108 bpm, BP 171/63 mmHg, RR 17/min, temp 98 F.
TMT was performed, showing ST depression at peak exercise. Rule out aortic stenosis.
Known polycystic ovary syndrome, currently under treatment. Patient was shifted to the ward after AVR.

62-year-old male admitted with excessive thirst, nausea and jaundice. Previously hospitalized with CAP in 2008. The patient's sister has cirrhosis. Result of LFTs is pending at the time of writing. Findings are consistent with appendicitis. Patient was shifted to the ward after ERCP.

Patient is a 31 year old male complaining of blurred vision and numbness since yesterday. The patient's sister has facial nerve palsy. Electroencephalogram was performed, showing a normal background rhythm. Findings are consistent with pneumothorax. Surgeons recommended burr hole drainage and lumbar puncture.

70-year-old female admitted with weight gain, wrist pain and inability to bear weight. On direct questioning, the patient admitted to hip pain. The patient did not experience difficulty breathing. Uric acid level was performed, showing a level of 5.1 mg/dL. Findings are consistent with ACL tear. Surgeons recommended closed reduction and POP cast.

74-year-old male admitted with vertigo, photophobia and resting tremor. There is a strong family history of transient ischemic attack. Patient is not on sumatriptan. Administered dexamethasone 10 mg intravenously in the department. Known peripheral neuropathy, currently under treatment. Surgeons recommended decompressive craniectomy and mechanical thrombectomy.
25-year-old female admitted with dyspnoea, coughing up blood and cough. Surgical history: NIV and bronchoscopy. Will proceed to bariatric surgery if CXR is abnormal.

Patient is a 38 year old male complaining of difficulty swallowing and palpitations since yesterday. On direct questioning, the patient admitted to loss of appetite. The patient did not experience icterus. Administered pantoprazole 40 mg intravenously in the department. Physical examination showed haematemesis; HR 73 bpm, BP 150/61 mmHg, RR 14/min, temp 100 F. Rule out peptic ulcer disease.

Patient is a 42 year old female complaining of numbness in the feet and hair loss since yesterday. On direct questioning, the patient admitted to oligomenorrhoea. Findings are consistent with vitamin D deficiency.

Patient is a 81 year old female complaining of melaena and vomiting since yesterday. Previous episodes of right iliac fossa pain in 2022 resolved without treatment. There is a strong family history of ulcerative colitis. Patient is on lactulose, 30 mL PO BID. Physical examination showed epigastric pain; SpO2 90% on room air, BP 143/70 mmHg, heart rate 115 bpm. Fecal calprotectin was performed, showing a value of 30 mcg/g. Surgeons recommended endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography and variceal banding.

Patient is a 65 year old female complaining of breathlessness on exertion and chest tightness since yesterday. Absence of haemoptysis noted. The patient's sister has pulmonary TB. Will proceed to CT-guided lung biopsy if sputum culture is abnormal.

55-year-old male admitted with burning micturition, deformity of the limb and LBP.
Absence of pallor noted.
Previous episodes of body aches in 2019 resolved without treatment. Administered telmisartan 40 mg orally in the department.
Physical examination showed shoulder pain; HR 81 bpm, BP 114/90 mmHg, RR 19/min, temp 102 F. Result of C-reactive protein is pending at the time of writing. Rule out hyponatremia. Surgeons recommended arthroscopy of the knee and haemodialysis. Will proceed to bone marrow biopsy if complete blood count is abnormal.
Patient is a 63 year old female complaining of left arm pain and dizziness since yesterday. The patient's sister has coronary artery disease. Patient is on metoprolol, 25 mg PO BID.

Patient is a 85 year old male complaining of chest pain and fainting episode since yesterday. Over the past few days the patient has had altered sensorium with occasional palpitations. Patient is not on isoniazid. Findings are consistent with pericarditis. Patient was shifted to the ward after coronary angiography.
Patient is a 52 year old male complaining of numbness and loss of consciousness since yesterday. Result of EEG is pending at the time of writing. Suspected ischaemic stroke versus ulcerative colitis.

Patient is a 60 year old male complaining of dizziness and weight loss since yesterday. Absence of pallor noted. Previous episodes of high-grade fever in 2000 resolved without treatment. Had a course of ferrous sulfate BID for 8 weeks two months ago with partial relief. Findings are consistent with high blood pressure. Surgical history: Foley catheterization and IV cannulation. Patient was shifted to the ward after LP.

55-year-old male admitted with morning stiffness, tiredness and lower back pain. On direct questioning, the patient admitted to knee pain. The patient did not experience numbness in the fingers. Previous episodes of joint tenderness in 1998 resolved without treatment.
The patient's sister has rotator cuff tear. Patient is on aspirin, 150 mg PO OD. Result of ECG is pending at the time of writing.
Suspected PCOS versus lumbar spondylosis. Known osteoarthritis of the knee, currently under treatment. Surgeons recommended total hip replacement and POP cast.
Will proceed to CPR if ESR is abnormal.

32-year-old male admitted with neck stiffness, nausea and weight loss. Had a course of ondansetron stat for 1 day two months ago with partial relief. Blood culture was performed, showing growth of a gram-negative organism. Surgical history: bone marrow biopsy and hemodialysis.

51-year-old male admitted with burning micturition, dyspnoea and headache. Absence of nausea noted. Patient is on paracetamol, 500 mg orally SOS. Physical examination showed pallor; HR 125 bpm, BP 168/65 mmHg, RR 18/min, temp 97 F. Urine R/M was performed, showing protein 2+ and no casts. Findings are consistent with PE. Surgical history: urinary catheterization and lumbar puncture.

38-year-old female admitted with neck stiffness, blurred vision and resting tremor. Over the past few days the patient has had weakness of the left arm with occasional night sweats. Absence of headache noted.
Previously hospitalized with transient ischaemic attack in 2005.
The patient's sister has intracerebral hemorrhage. Had a course of levetiracetam twice daily for 6 months two months ago with partial relief. Administered levodopa-carbidopa 100/25 mg orally in the department. Physical examination showed dysarthria; HR 115 bpm, BP 125/92 mmHg, RR 15/min, temp 102 F. Suspected peripheral neuropathy versus GBS. Known ischaemic stroke, currently under treatment. Surgeons recommended decompressive craniectomy and chest drain insertion.

62-year-old male admitted with profuse sweating, difficulty breathing and altered mental status. On direct questioning, the patient admitted to loss of appetite. There is a strong family history of organophosphate poisoning. Had a course of ondansetron stat for 1 day two months ago with partial relief.

Patient is a 87 year old male complaining of fatigue and giddiness since yesterday. Patient is on co-amoxiclav, 625 mg PO three times daily. Triage vitals were as follows: HR 107 bpm, BP 141/104 mmHg, RR 28/min, temp 98 F. Result of ESR is pending at the time of writing. Known enteric fever, currently under treatment.

53-year-old male admitted with hoarseness of voice, dyspnoea and pleuritic chest pain. On direct questioning, the patient admitted to fever.
The patient did not experience blurred vision. Previously hospitalized with bronchiectasis in 2007. There is a strong family history of acute pancreatitis.
Administered hydrocortisone 100 mg intravenously in the department. Physical examination showed muscle weakness; SpO2 96% on room air, BP 132/93 mmHg, heart rate 64 bpm. Result of USG abdomen is pending at the time of writing. Suspected pulmonary TB versus bronchial asthma.
Findings are consistent with pulmonary embolism.
Surgical history: radioactive iodine ablation and CT-guided lung biopsy. Patient was shifted to the ward after thyroidectomy.

Patient is a 81 year old male complaining of PND and diaphoresis since yesterday. On direct questioning, the patient admitted to left arm pain. Previously hospitalized with coronary artery disease in 2013. Had a course of furosemide twice daily for 2 days two months ago with partial relief. Result of lipid profile is pending at the time of writing. Suspected aortic stenosis versus myocardial infarction. Known CHF, currently under treatment.

63-year-old male admitted with polydipsia, cold intolerance and hair loss. The patient did not experience blurred vision. Physical examination showed muscle weakness; HR 108 bpm, BP 179/70 mmHg, RR 21/min, temp 103 F. 25-hydroxy vitamin D level was performed, showing a level of 11 ng/mL.

48-year-old female admitted with muscle weakness, fine tremor and unintentional weight loss.
Over the past few days the patient has had constipation with occasional excessive thirst. The patient did not experience numbness in the feet. Previous episodes of paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea in 2017 resolved without treatment. Patient is not on glimepiride. Patient is on insulin glargine, 14 units SC at bedtime. Physical examination showed fatigue; SpO2 91% on room air, BP 136/100 mmHg, heart rate 70 bpm. Fasting blood glucose was performed, showing a value of 168 mg/dL. Suspected osteoporosis versus T1DM. Surgeons recommended sleeve gastrectomy and surgical wound debridement. Patient was shifted to the ward after lung biopsy.

Patient is a 79 year old female complaining of polyuria and heartburn since yesterday. Previous episodes of excessive thirst in 1999 resolved without treatment. Findings are consistent with DKA. Surgeons recommended radioiodine therapy and parathyroidectomy.

59-year-old male admitted with syncope, SOB and difficulty walking.
Over the past few days the patient has had sweating with occasional dizziness. The patient did not experience palpitations. Previously hospitalized with hyperlipidaemia in 2008.
There is a strong family history of hypertension.
Administered levodopa-carbidopa 100/25 mg orally in the department. Triage vitals were as follows: HR 113 bpm, BP 105/99 mmHg, RR 24/min, temp 97 F.
TFTs was performed, showing a high thyrotropin level with a low free thyroxine level.
Suspected aortic stenosis versus unstable angina. Findings are consistent with heart attack.
Surgical history: aortic valve replacement and angioplasty.
Will proceed to electrical cardioversion if NT-proBNP is abnormal.

21-year-old male admitted with fainting episode, jaundice and loose stools. Over the past few days the patient has had abdominal distension with occasional dysphagia. Previous episodes of melena in 2016 resolved without treatment. Patient is on colchicine, 0.5 mg orally BID. Physical examination showed loss of appetite; SpO2 92% on room air, BP 155/92 mmHg, heart rate 76 bpm. Widal test was performed, showing a significant titre of 1:160. Known IBS, currently under treatment.

Patient is a 85 year old female complaining of bleeding from the wound and knee pain since yesterday.
On direct questioning, the patient admitted to profuse sweating. Previous episodes of seizure in 2020 resolved without treatment. There is a strong family history of fracture of the femur. Patient is not on tiotropium. Administered apixaban 2.5 mg orally in the department. Physical examination showed haematemesis; SpO2 96% on room air, BP 163/67 mmHg, heart rate 110 bpm. Urine drug screen was performed, showing a negative result.
Suspected TBI versus acute pancreatitis. Surgeons recommended splint application and coronary stent placement. Will proceed to endotracheal intubation if ABG is abnormal.

Patient is a 76 year old male complaining of blurred vision and unintentional weight loss since yesterday. Over the past few days the patient has had muscle weakness with occasional excessive thirst. Previous episodes of tremors in 1999 resolved without treatment. The patient's sister has DKA. Administered insulin aspart 8 units subcutaneously in the department. Suspected hypertension versus type 1 diabetes mellitus. Surgeons recommended parathyroidectomy and fine needle aspiration cytology.

30-year-old male admitted with chest pain, seizure and bleeding from the wound. The patient's sister has traumatic brain injury. Administered salbutamol 100 mcg via inhaler in the department. Triage vitals were as follows: SpO2 92% on room air, BP 100/73 mmHg, heart rate 81 bpm. Result of ABG is pending at the time of writing. Suspected anaphylaxis versus fracture of the femur.

25-year-old male admitted with profuse sweating, high-grade fever and hematemesis. Absence of severe abdominal pain noted.
Previously hospitalized with aortic stenosis in 2018.
There is a strong family history of acute pancreatitis. Patient is not on domperidone. Triage vitals were as follows: SpO2 95% on room air, BP 160/90 mmHg, heart rate 118 bpm.
Electrocardiogram was performed, showing ST depression in the anterior leads. Suspected HTN versus sepsis.
Patient was shifted to the ward after splint application.

Patient is a 21 year old male complaining of vomiting and haematemesis since yesterday. The patient's sister has pneumothorax. Surgeons recommended bariatric surgery and non-invasive ventilation. Patient was shifted to the ward after mechanical thrombectomy.

Patient is a 75 year old male complaining of hemiparesis and vertigo since yesterday. Over the past few days the patient has had numbness with occasional blurred vision. The patient did not experience loss of consciousness. Previous episodes of facial droop in 2024 resolved without treatment. There is a strong family history of epilepsy. Triage vitals were as follows: SpO2 98% on room air, BP 164/99 mmHg, heart rate 66 bpm. Result of sputum culture is pending at the time of writing.

60-year-old male admitted with hair loss, knee pain and morning stiffness. The patient did not experience inability to bear weight. There is a strong family history of IBS. Physical examination showed radiating leg pain; HR 123 bpm, BP 157/76 mmHg, RR 22/min, temp 101 F. Result of knee X-ray is pending at the time of writing. Suspected ulcerative colitis versus carpal tunnel syndrome.

63-year-old female admitted with weakness of the left arm, vertigo and photophobia. There is a strong family history of T2DM. Triage vitals were as follows: SpO2 98% on room air, BP 141/99 mmHg, heart rate 77 bpm. Carotid Doppler was performed, showing 60% narrowing of the right internal carotid artery.

54-year-old male admitted with heartburn, excessive thirst and black tarry stools. Previous episodes of loose stools in 1998 resolved without treatment. The patient's sister has liver cirrhosis. Patient is not on metronidazole.

Patient is a 45 year old male complaining of paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea and palpitations since yesterday.
On direct questioning, the patient admitted to sweating. The patient did not experience shortness of breath. Previously hospitalized with pericarditis in 2011. Had a course of furosemide every morning for 2 weeks two months ago with partial relief. Administered atorvastatin 80 mg PO in the department. Triage vitals were as follows: HR 58 bpm, BP 111/104 mmHg, RR 28/min, temp 102 F. Serum troponin was performed, showing a value of 0.01 ng/mL. Suspected acute pancreatitis versus DVT. Known AFib, currently under treatment. Surgical history: electrical cardioversion and angioplasty. Patient was shifted to the ward after coronary angiography.

85-year-old female admitted with wrist pain, joint tenderness and seizure. Over the past few days the patient has had inability to bear weight with occasional hip pain. Administered colchicine 0.5 mg orally in the department.

74-year-old male admitted with nausea, unintentional weight loss and loss of consciousness. On direct questioning, the patient admitted to hematemesis. Administered metformin 500 mg orally in the department. Triage vitals were as follows: HR 117 bpm, BP 143/76 mmHg, RR 19/min, temp 103 F. Suspected intracerebral haemorrhage versus enteric fever. Known malaria, currently under treatment. Patient was shifted to the ward after IV cannulation.

83-year-old female admitted with joint tenderness, poor appetite and left arm pain. Absence of dysuria noted. Physical examination showed nausea; HR 77 bpm, BP 154/64 mmHg, RR 20/min, temp 98 F. Result of complete blood count is pending at the time of writing. Known IDA, currently under treatment. Surgical history: packed red cell transfusion and bone marrow biopsy. Will proceed to LP if malaria rapid antigen test is abnormal.

65-year-old female admitted with loss of appetite, heartburn and vomiting. Previously hospitalized with PUD in 2011. Administered metronidazole 400 mg PO in the department. Stool examination was performed, showing numerous pus cells and no ova. Rule out acute appendicitis. Findings are consistent with acute pancreatitis.

58-year-old male admitted with loss of appetite, bloating and icterus. On direct questioning, the patient admitted to right iliac fossa pain. Previous episodes of melena in 2016 resolved without treatment. Result of liver function tests is pending at the time of writing. Rule out gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Findings are consistent with cholelithiasis. Patient was shifted to the ward after upper GI endoscopy.

30-year-old female admitted with syncope, morning stiffness and chest pain. Absence of left arm pain noted. Triage vitals were as follows: SpO2 90% on room air, BP 126/65 mmHg, heart rate 58 bpm. Treadmill test was performed, showing ST depression at peak exercise. Suspected asthma versus aortic stenosis. Surgical history: POP cast and pacemaker implantation. Will proceed to CABG if serum troponin is abnormal.

Patient is a 24 year old female complaining of breathlessness on exertion and chest tightness since yesterday. Findings are consistent with lung cancer. Surgical history: NIV and intercostal drain insertion.
